{{Quote|Not bad, little Ewok. But I've got more bad luck for you!|Teebo's lucksprite, as he tries to sabotage Wicket W. Warrick's rescue of Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka|<ref name="JML" />}}
'''Lucksprites''' were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings found on the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]]. According to [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] belief, the creatures were responsible for the good or ill fortune of every being on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]]. In practice, a [[luck]]sprite could indeed affect someone's luck via blasts of iridescent energy projected from a prehensile tentacle growing from the top of its head. Lucksprites were otherwise [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] in shape, although their [[Limb/Legends|legs]] were much shorter than their arms, and their heads were large in proportion to the rest of their body. Other key physical features included large, pointed [[Ear/Legends|ears]] and drooping [[Eye/Legends|eyelids]]. The creatures were divided into two camps, those who caused good luck, and those who brought on bad luck. Lucksprites could take great pleasure in using their chance-changing abilities.

[[Teebo's lucksprite|One lucksprite]] made a nuisance of itself in [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]] around [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]]. Because the Ewok [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Wystri Warrick]] was having difficulty preparing for his [[Soldier/Legends|warrior's]] test, an ordeal designed to test his aptitude to enter that profession, Warrick's friend [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]] secured the services of a lucksprite. Little did he know that it was a ''bad'' lucksprite; the creature foiled Warrick's chances and sent the Ewok into melancholy. Nevertheless, Warrick's friends forced the lucksprite to admit its meddling to their saddened comrade. An [[Unidentified Endor arachnid|arachnid creature]] attacked during the confession, and the lucksprite did its best to prevent Warrick from overcoming the new obstacle. Nevertheless, the Ewok prevailed, causing the lucksprite to enter a depression of its own.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Lucksprite_tentacle_head.png|thumb|left|200px|Lucksprites shot sparkling blasts of luck from a tentacle atop their heads.]]
Lucksprites were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] beings, with two [[Limb/Legends|arms]], two legs, and a head. The arms were long and wiry, considerably lengthier than the short, thin legs<ref name="JML" /> that stood the beings roughly 0.66 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] from the ground.<ref name="height" /> Two four-fingered hands were attached to each arm, and two long, narrow feet to each leg. These limbs surrounded the torso and abdomen, which converged in a single squat, round mass.<ref name="JML" />

Atop the lucksprite's long, thin neck sat an oversized head, wider than it was tall and with no appreciable chin. A broad, thick-lipped mouth stretched from one side of the face to the other, revealing a [[Color/Legends|red]] interior and pink tongue when opened. Above the mouth sat a wide, oblong nose with perpetually flared nostrils. This rested below two wide-set, yellow [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], which peered from beneath droopy lids. Both sides of the face were flanked by two huge, triangular [[Ear/Legends|ears]] with pink interiors. In at least [[Teebo's lucksprite|one case]], the back of these sensory organs and the rest of the lucksprite's skin was green.<ref name="JML" />

Growing from the top of the head, each lucksprite had a fat, tentacular appendage whose prehensility allowed the lucksprite to move it at will. This organ shot bolts of good or bad [[luck]]&mdash;depending on its owner's proclivities&mdash;that affected their target's performance of various tasks. These salvos of serendipity appeared as clouds of [[Gold/Legends|golden]] sparkles. Each discharge of this energy was accompanied by a ''zap'' sound.<ref name="JML" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|You know, I love my work.|Teebo's bad lucksprite|<ref name="JML" />}}
[[File:Lucksprite_buddy_buddy.png|thumb|right|200px|Lucksprites could bestow both positive and negative luck, hiding their true nature from their target until it suited them.]]
Lucksprites were divided into two groups: good lucksprites and bad lucksprites.<ref name="JML" /> Each type had the ability to bestow both flavors of luck on other beings, but the lucksprites strongly preferred one or the other depending on their individual temperaments.<ref name="CSWE II 264">{{CSWECite|II|264|lucksprite}}</ref> This could prove either a help or hindrance to the target depending on whether the lucksprite conveyed helpful or harmful fortune. In some instances, a lucksprite might agree to work for someone, bestowing luck as the patron requested. Lucksprites could take great pride in such work, cuddling up to their employers and laughing as they fulfilled their duties. Should a lucksprite's target manage to overcome the weal or woe bestowed upon them&mdash;succeeding in a task that a bad lucksprite attempted to curse, for example&mdash;the lucksprite could grow despondent at the perceived failure. Lucksprites also had the ability to teleport, a tactic they occasionally employed to avoid angry victims of their luck-inducing abilities.<ref name="JML" />

Lucksprites were capable of learning and speaking [[Ewokese/Legends|Ewokese]]. Their large mouths expressed a wide variety of emotions, including smiling or frowning.<ref name="JML" /> In the folklore of the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] of the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]], lucksprites were viewed as powerful beings who presided over the good or ill fortune of all creatures on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]].<ref name="CSWE II 264" />

At least one lucksprite wore a tunic over tights. This being tied this ensemble with a [[Rope/Legends|rope]] belt. The lucksprite hid its head tentacle under a pointed [[Hat/Legends|cap]] and could wrap itself in a cloth to appear as a sack, leaving only the eyes to peer out and betray its true nature.<ref name="JML" />

==History==
{{Quote|Worry no more, Wicket, buddy! Luck is on your side. Ta-da! I brought you this lucksprite, so you can ''re''lax, so you'll have luck for your test tomorrow.|Teebo|<ref name="JML" />}}
[[File:Presenting_the_lucksprite.png|thumb|left|200px|Teebo presented a lucksprite to help Wicket W. Warrick complete his skills test.]]
By [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> lucksprites had entered Ewok legend.<ref name="CSWE II 264" /> Sometime around that [[Galactic Standard Calendar|year]],<ref name="time">Although "[[Just My Luck]]" takes place in 3 ABY, the sequence of events in which the lucksprite appears take place at an unspecified point in this year or earlier.</ref> the young Ewoks of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]] were taking skills tests to determine their aptitude for their chosen professions. To help his friend, [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Wystri Warrick]], who was practicing for the test to become a [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]], the Ewok [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]] secured the services of a lucksprite for the would-be warrior's test day. During a practice session, the lucksprite blessed Warrick with good fortune: not only did the Ewok fire three [[Arrow/Legends|arrows]] directly into a target, he also split the target&mdash;and the [[Tree/Legends|tree]] on which it hung&mdash;in two.<ref name="JML" />

The day of Warrick's skills test, however, the lucksprite showed its true colors. When the Ewok used a pole to vault up to a tree, the pole snapped, sending him tumbling. When Warrick swung on a vine to grab a doll from a tree, the lucksprite zapped a [[Unidentified spiny Endorian creature|spiny creature]] nearby so that the Ewok would grab it instead; the pain caused Warrick to fall from the trees, dislodge a fallen log, and topple the [[Judge/Legends|judges]]' platform where his [[Council of Elders (Ewok)/Legends|elders]] were observing his performance. The blunder cost Warrick his chance to be a warrior; in fact, his [[City/Legends|village]] [[Chief/Legends|chief]], [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]], assigned him to be an apprentice [[Bordok/Legends|bordok]] stable sweeper instead. The lucksprite then admitted to Warrick's friends&mdash;Teebo, [[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka/Legends|Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka]], and [[Latara/Legends|Latara]]&mdash;that it was, in fact, a ''bad'' lucksprite. The creature then disappeared on the back of a bordok-driven [[cart]], a vehicle that it caused to nearly run the Ewoks over as it passed.<ref name="JML" />

Teebo tracked the lucksprite down and brought it to confront Warrick at the [[Cavern of Broken Dreams]], where the despondent Ewok had gone to sulk. When an [[Unidentified Endor arachnid|arachnid creature]] emerged from the cave and pursued Kneesaa, the lucksprite got up to its antics again: it shot Kneesaa with ill fortune to make her drop her lasso, with which she hoped to capture the creature. Teebo and Latara attacked the mischievous creature, but the lucksprite simply teleported out of harm's way. Kneesaa, meanwhile, fell into the [[Spider/Legends|arachnid's]] web, which stretched across a deep chasm.<ref name="JML" />

With Kneesaa in danger, Warrick snapped out of his stupor. He snatched Kneesaa from the web and put her on his shoulders. As he crossed a tightrope back to the ledge, the lucksprite shot the rope and snapped it, forcing Warrick to grab the rope and swing across. Teebo sneaked up behind the lucksprite and covered it with its own hat, preventing it from using its luck-bestowing tentacle and from seeing the goings-on. Without the meddlesome lucksprite's interference, Warrick swung to safety, destroyed the web with a large stone, and caused the arachnid to plummet into the canyon.<ref name="JML" />

Afterward, the bad lucksprite was depressed to have been foiled. It claimed that no Ewok warrior had ever managed to break its bad luck, but somehow Wicket W. Warrick had. Warrick, cheered to hear that he had succeeded where others had failed, offered the lucksprite a job as an apprentice stable sweeper.<ref name="JML" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[Michael Dubil]] wrote the first and only ''[[Star Wars]]'' story to feature a lucksprite to date, the [[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']] episode "[[Just My Luck]]." The cartoon first aired on [[November 22]], [[1986]], during the [[Ewoks: Season Two|second season]] of ''Ewoks''.<ref name="SWC">{{InsiderCite|27|A Star Wars CELibration|A ''Star Wars'' CELibration}}</ref> Although the lucksprite has several lines in the episode, the voice actor who played him was uncredited.<ref name="JML" />
